title: Natural finite pullback comparison of strict reduction towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ use the small pro-etale site, the completed ring sheaf $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/t^n)_W$, the constant quotient sheaves $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$ and the unbounded derived category $D(R_W)$ of sheaves of $R_W$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All quotient modules are restricted to $R_W$ along the specified limit projections. Let $g:T'\to T$ be any morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Write $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$ for the map induced by the finite projections and $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}R_{T'}$ for ordinary ringed-topos module pullback. Use the strict reduction functor $K\mapsto K_\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and the derived strict tower pullback $V_g=Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K\in D(R_T)$ put $P_n=P\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n}$ and
$$B_g(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*P_n,$$
with the actual quotient transitions; $g_n^*$ is the exact finite-coefficient module pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. This strict tower construction descends to a functor $B_g:D(R_T)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_{R_{T'}})$, and there is a natural isomorphism of functors
$$b_g:V_g\circ(-)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g.$$
Its specified value on $P$ is represented by the strict-tower zigzag
$$G(P\otimes Q_{T,\bullet})\xrightarrow{\sim}(GP\otimes Q_{T',n})_n\longrightarrow(GP\otimes S_{T',n})_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g(P),$$
where $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$, transition $(t,1)$, and the middle arrow is the quotient augmentation. Here $GP$ and every $G(P\otimes Q_{T,n})$ are K-flat with flat terms and the middle arrow is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. The last arrow is the balanced isomorphism identifying both sides with $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}S_{T',n}$; on tensor sections it sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes\bar b a$, with inverse inserting $1$. All scalar maps are the components of $c_g$, so these are exactly the finite evaluation comparisons fixed in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-a1-integral-completed-pullback-interfaces]. For each $r\in\mathbf Z$ these maps commute with the standard termwise tensor and pullback shifts, and hence
$$s^B_{K,r}\circ b_{g,K[r]}=b_{g,K}[r]\circ s^V_{K,r},$$
where $s^V:V_g((K[r])_\bullet)\to V_g(K_\bullet)[r]$ and $s^B:B_g(K[r])\to B_g(K)[r]$ are the reduction/tower-pullback and finite termwise shift comparisons, respectively. The naturality is for all derived morphisms and is independent of representatives, without assuming that $c_g$ is invertible or that $G$ is exact.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes over $R_T$. On all complexes define $B_g^0(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*(P\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n})$, using the quotient transitions and their compatible coefficient maps. This additive construction commutes with shifts and mapping-cone complexes: it acts on each differential and each of the two summands of a cone. A quasi-isomorphism between objects of $\mathcal P_T$ remains a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with each $S_{T,n}$ by change of rings, and then after $g_n^*$ by finite-coefficient exactness. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. Exactness in towers is levelwise, so $B_g^0$ takes these quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms of tower complexes. Flat-term K-flat resolutions exist for every complex. The resolving-class theorem therefore supplies an everywhere defined functor $B_g:D(R_T)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_{R_{T'}})$, with its canonical computation isomorphism $B_g(QP)\cong Q B_g^0(P)$ for $P\in\mathcal P_T$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YT/06YY (change-of-rings quasi-isomorphism invariance), and derived.tex 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes); finite exactness as cited.

proof.text: For $P\in\mathcal P_T$ put $F(P)=(P\otimes S_{T,n})_n$ and $H(P)=(P\otimes Q_{T,n})_n$. The principal-Koszul strict replacement lemma gives a natural strict quasi-isomorphism $a_P:H(P)\to F(P)$ whose source levels are K-flat with flat terms. Its source transitions are $1_P\otimes(t,1)$ and its target transitions are the actual quotients. Thus $QF(P)$ is the specified reduction tower $(QP)_\bullet$. By the definition of $V_g$ and its diagram resolving class, $GH(P)$ computes $V_g((QP)_\bullet)$: use $V_g(Qa_P)^{-1}$ followed by the computation isomorphism at $H(P)$. These identifications are natural for chain maps $P\to P'$. The index category is the small category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the diagram replacement statement applies.

source.place: Tag 06YS and the strict principal-Koszul replacement; Tag 06YY and the small-diagram construction specified in completed pullback.

proof.text: Apply preservation of K-flat complexes with flat terms under ringed-topos pullback to $(g,c_g)$, first to $P$ and then to each $P\otimes Q_{T,n}$ supplied in Step 2. It follows that $GP$ and every $G(P\otimes Q_{T,n})$ are K-flat with flat terms. The morphism of topoi is presented by the chosen small pro-etale sites, and $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$ is a map of commutative ring sheaves, precisely the hypotheses of that preservation theorem. This argument imposes no flatness or invertibility condition on $c_g$.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), as included in the ringed-topoi tensor/pullback statement.

proof.text: The ordinary cochain tensor comparison gives $G(P\otimes Q_{T,n})\cong GP\otimes GQ_{T,n}$. Under the action unitor $GR_T\cong R_{T'}$, the map $G(t^n)$ is multiplication by $t^n$: the components defining $c_g$ preserve the constant scalar $t$. Consequently $GQ_{T,n}\cong Q_{T',n}$. These isomorphisms identify $G(t,1)$ with $(t,1)$ and hence give the first isomorphism of strict towers in the statement, not just separate isomorphisms of derived evaluations. The cochain comparison is natural and respects action unitors; no quasi-isomorphism preservation is needed for this ordinary chain isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03EL (sites-modules, lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); cochain comparison and action unitors.

proof.text: Apply the principal-Koszul strict replacement lemma on $T'$ to the complex $GP$, whose flat-term K-flat hypotheses were checked in Step 3. It gives the strict quotient augmentation $(GP\otimes Q_{T',n})_n\to(GP\otimes S_{T',n})_n$, and every component is a quasi-isomorphism. Levelwise exactness in the tower category makes this a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes. This proves the assertion about the middle arrow; it does not result from applying the possibly nonexact functor $G$ to an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Principal-Koszul augmentation over the target completed coefficient sheaf; Tag 02MZ (homology, lemma-inverse-systems-abelian).

proof.text: Put $R=R_T$, $R'=R_{T'}$, $S_n=S_{T,n}$ and $S'_n=S_{T',n}$. Finite constant coefficient transport identifies $g^{-1}S_n$ with $S'_n$. The coefficient square commutes because $\pi'_n c_g$ is, by definition, $g^{-1}R\to g^{-1}S_n\to S'_n$. Apply the cochain scalar-association comparison to $R\to S_n$, $R'\to S'_n$ and this square. Both $GP\otimes_{R'}S'_n$ and $g_n^*(P\otimes_R S_n)$ identify with $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}R}S'_n$. On the first the identification is $(x\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes\pi'_n(b)a$, with inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. On the second it is $(x\otimes z)\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes c_{g,n}(z)a$, with inverse inserting $1$ in the $g^{-1}S_n$ factor. The commuting coefficient square makes these formulas balanced; the two composites are identities by the tensor relations. The formulas commute with restrictions and degreewise differentials and therefore induce inverse maps of sheaf tensor complexes. Composing the first identification with the inverse of the second gives the last isomorphism in the statement.

source.place: Tags 03EK (sites-modules, section-tensor-product) and 03EL; scalar-association map kappa in the cochain coherence statement.

proof.text: All formulas of Step 6 commute with quotient transitions. For example reducing $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ from level $n+1$ to $n$ gives $x\otimes q'_{n+1,n}(\pi'_{n+1}(b)a)=x\otimes\pi'_n(b)q'_{n+1,n}(a)$ along either path. The corresponding formula on the finite pullback side follows from $q'c_{g,n+1}=c_{g,n}g^{-1}q$. Together with Step 4 this proves strictness of the entire displayed zigzag. Let $C_n:G(P\otimes S_n)\cong B_g^0(P)_n$ be the same scalar-association map. The zigzag at level $n$ is also $C_nG(a_{P,n})$: on a degree-zero Koszul generator the augmentation is the quotient $R\to S_n$, and on the degree-minus-one generator it is zero. On the inverse-image quotient-unit generator $b\otimes g^{-1}(x\otimes1)$, $C_n$ gives the finite pullback generator with scalar $\pi'_n(b)$. This is exactly the pure-tensor and K-flat representative normalization of the fixed interface. Hence evaluation of our zigzag is the specified finite comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism with the same source and target.

proof.text: Every arrow constructed in Steps 2 and 4--7 is natural in a chain map $f:P\to P'$: its local tensor formulas replace $x$ by $g^{-1}f(x)$ on both paths. The augmentation is $1\otimes\epsilon_n$, so it has the same property. Thus they define a natural isomorphism between the restrictions of $V_g\circ(-)_\bullet$ and $B_g$ to the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat complexes. These functors already exist on derived categories by Step 1 and the specified tower definitions. The localization equivalence $W_T^{-1}\mathcal P_T\simeq D(R_T)$ in the site tensor-descent statement extends this natural isomorphism uniquely. Explicitly the chain-map naturality equation for a quasi-isomorphism $s$ can be multiplied by the two inverse images of $s$ to give naturality for $s^{-1}$; the equivalence says these localized maps give all derived morphisms. Every object has a representative in $\mathcal P_T$, so all components are invertible. This defines $b_g$, proves naturality for all derived morphisms, and proves independence of representatives. Each map is $R_{T'}$-linear by its balanced formula.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 0G7D (lemma-factor-through-K-flat), via the flat-term K-flat localization equivalence; the displayed natural cochain maps.

proof.text: Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$. The tensor comparison extracting a shift from the first argument is unsigned: $(P[r]\otimes Q_{T,n})\cong(P\otimes Q_{T,n})[r]$ sends each tensor to itself in the reindexed summand. For $x$ of degree $p$ in $P[r]$, its differential is $(-1)^r dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ on both sides, since the shifted total differential has second coefficient $(-1)^r(-1)^{p+r}=(-1)^p$. The same comparison applies to $S_n[0]$. Termwise $G$ and $g_n^*$ commute with shifts by the identity on terms. The balanced maps, the quotient augmentation and the transitions have degree zero, so the resulting shift squares for every arrow of the zigzag commute already as chain maps. The canonical resolving-class shift comparisons for reduction and $V_g$ are computed by these termwise shifts; flat-term K-flat classes are stable under them. Thus on $\mathcal P_T$ the resulting equality is $s^B_{K,r}b_{g,K[r]}=b_{g,K}[r]s^V_{K,r}$. The localization equivalence of Step 8 extends this equality to every $K$. This proves precisely the asserted shift compatibility for all integers.
